newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish crude oil import prices soar in October.
newsitem.headline: Finnish crude oil import prices soar in October.

text.p: Finnish import prices of energy minerals, primarily crude oil, soared 42.9 percent year-on-year in October to post the steepest year-on-year climb in any month during the 1990s, Statistics Finland (SF) said on Monday.
Energy mineral import prices rose 4.6 percent in October from September, SF said in a statement.

Pushed higher by firming world market prices for crude oil, the rise in energy minerals import prices has accelerated from 8.6 percent year-on-year in June to 23.6 percent in July, 26.2 percent in August and 30.8 percent in September, an SF official said by telephone.

The import price index rose 0.6 percent in October from September and the year-on-year rise was 3.3 percent. SF said the rise was due largely to more expensive crude oil, petroleum products, machinery and equipment and vehicles.
Import prices of raw materials and production necessities rose 4.3 percent year-on-year, investment goods import prices rose 2.9 percent and consumer goods import prices rose 1.7 percent.
More expensive petroleum products also boosted Finnish wholesale prices in October, SF said.
These, coupled with agriculture and forestry products wholesale prices took the index to a 0.7-percent rise compared with September. Year-on-year, wholesale prices rose 1.2 percent.

Wholesale prices of energy minerals were up 37.8 percent, in line with the rise in crude oil import prices. Lacking natural resources of its own, Finland -- primarily state-controlled oil, chemicals and energy group Neste Oy -- imports all its crude oil.
